question.problem: Consider the function $g(x,y)=4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}.$ What is the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(2,1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=⟨5,12⟩?$

current_example.problem: Consider the function $g (x, y) = \ln \left(\sqrt {xy^3}\right).$ What is the rate of change of $g$ at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ in the direction in which the function increases most rapidly?
current_example.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $\nabla g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)\!\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x{y}^{3}})),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}\cdot \frac{{y}^{3}}{2\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}},\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}\cdot \frac{3x{y}^{2}}{2\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2x},\,\frac{3}{2y}⟩ \\ ∇g(\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}) & =⟨\frac{1}{2\cdot (\frac{1}{2})},\frac{3}{2\cdot (\frac{3}{2})}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ in the direction of $\nabla g\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖∇g(\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2})‖ & =‖⟨1,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
